subject: Cloud routing & unit-econ follow-up — next tests and action plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@greenline.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Cloud routing & unit-econ follow-up — next tests and action plan

Hi Tom and Priya,

Thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum.

TL;DR
- Redwood appears to match your functional needs from the demo. The main open items are cost modeling against your current hyperscaler spend and an apples-to-apples production replay to validate latency and cache hit assumptions.
- Attached: a conservative per-1M token breakdown and a draft test spec for a 24h replay.

What we heard from you
- Predominantly short completion calls, median request length ~120 tokens, 70% of traffic is repeat prefixes from product search flows.
- Target latency p95 under 220 ms for interactive product lookups.
- Current vendor mix: Vertex for embeddings, Bedrock variants for generation in bursty spikes. You want a single inference path or a clear routing policy to lower ops overhead.

Redwood differentiators relevant to this eval
- Cost-aware routing: can direct low-cost traffic to quantized variants and reserve higher-precision models for tail queries.
- Transparent per-token economics and simulated batching estimates so you can see the per-1M token delta at different batch sizes and cache hit rates.
- Built-in KV/prefix cache that we can instrument to emulate your 70% repeat-prefix workload and surface cache hit metrics in the Console.

Proposed next tests (actionable)
1) 24h production-like replay against your anonymized traces (we only need a sample) to measure: p50/p95 latency, realized batch sizes, token volume, and cache hit rate. Outcome: cost delta vs your current stack.
2) Targeted batch sizing sweep: run the same replay with batch sizes of 1, 8, 32 to show marginal per-token cost improvements and latency tradeoffs.
3) Routing scenario: emulate a mixed routing policy where 60% of traffic uses quantized model A and 40% uses full-precision model B to assess quality and cost.

Deliverables and timing
- Redwood provides test harness, expected compute credits, and a results deck within 5 business days after receiving the trace sample.
- We will instrument Console dashboards for your account so your engineers see cache hit rate and per-route token costs.

Next steps
- Tom/Priya: share a 24h anonymized trace sample or a synthetic 24h sample by Wed 03/03.
- Redwood: Ben will provision the test environment and Marissa will own post-test cost deck. Ben, can you confirm the expected compute credit ask?

Attachments: redwood_per_1M_token_breakdown_v1.xlsx, proposed-test-specs-24h-replay.json

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@greenline.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@greenline.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud routing & unit-econ follow-up — next tests and action plan

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we pull the trace:

1) Per-1M token calc: the attached spreadsheet looks to assume 50 token prompt and 200 token completion averages. Our medians are closer to 120 total tokens per request (we gave an example on the call). Can you rerun the per-1M with 120 as baseline?

2) Cache behavior: our traffic is largely repeat prefixes but with slight variations. Is the test harness able to parameterize match fuzziness so we can see hit rates at 70%, 60%, and 50%?

3) Run costs: what does Redwood expect for the compute credit allotment for the 24h replay with our volume? We want an up-front number so we can budget the PoC.

Also, one ask: can you show a quick comparison vs Bedrock's c7gn variants and Vertex's multi-region endpoints in the cost deck? We need to justify a migration path to our finance team.

Tom
VP of Product, Greenline Analytics

Subject: Re: Cloud routing & unit-econ follow-up — next tests and action plan

Hey Tom — quick answers and commitment from our side.

1) Per-1M token recalculation
We will regenerate the per-1M token workbook using 120 tokens/request as the baseline. That will update the per-1M generator/completion split and show both quantized and FP variants. Expect v2 by EOD PDT today.

2) Cache fuzziness and hit rate sweep
Our test harness supports configurable prefix-match thresholds and a parameter called fuzzy_match_pct which we can sweep to emulate 50/60/70% effective hit rates. The harness will report exact matched prefixes and effective hit rate.

3) Compute credits for the 24h replay
Based on the trace volume you described, we estimate the run will consume ~18 GPU-hours on a balanced mix of quantized and FP variants. For the PoC we can cover the first 24 GPU-hours under a trial credit; beyond that we typically invoice or request a small compute commitment. I will include exact numbers in the v2 workbook.

4) Hyperscaler comparison in the deck
We can include a modeled comparison vs Bedrock c7gn-class pricing and Vertex regional endpoints. We will call out assumed throughput/latency baselines for both vendors so the finance team has an apples-to-apples view.

Mutual action plan (short)
- Tue 03/02: Greenline shares trace sample (or synthetic) and confirms target p95 latency constraint.
- Wed 03/03 to Thu 03/04: Redwood executes 24h replay and batch sweep.
- Fri 03/05: Redwood deliverables — v2 per-1M workbook, test results deck, and a short findings call.

Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
